( d ) Calibrate all oil and gas flow meters that are used to measure liquid and gaseous feedstock volumes and flow rates (except for gas billing meters) according to the monitoring and QA/QC requirements for the Tier 3 methodology in § 98.34(b)(1) . Perform oil tank drop measurements (if used to quantify feedstock volumes) according to § 98.34(b)(2) . ( e ) For quality assurance and quality control of the supplier data, on an annual basis, you must measure the carbon contents of a representative sample of the feedstocks consumed using the appropriate ASTM Method as listed in paragraphs (c)(1) through (c)(8) of this section. ( f ) You may use company records or an engineering estimate to determine the annual ammonia production and the annual methanol production. ( g ) If CO 2 from ammonia production is used to produce urea at the same facility, you must determine the quantity of urea produced using methods or plant instruments used for accounting purposes (such as sales records). You must document the procedures used to ensure the accuracy of the estimates of urea produced. [ 74 FR 56374 , Oct. 30, 2009, as amended at 75 FR 79156 , Dec. 17, 2010; 81 FR 89253 , Dec. 9, 2016] § 98.75 Procedures for estimating missing data. A complete record of all measured parameters used in the GHG emissions calculations is required. Therefore, whenever the monitoring and quality assurance procedures in § 98.74 cannot be followed (e.g., if a meter malfunctions during unit operation), a substitute data value for the missing parameter shall be used in the calculations following paragraphs (a) and (b) of this section.
